elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 27.2 reads: "This Agreement is governed by New York law, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County." The original 27.2, which directed all courts and tribunals to disregard the indicia of any particular municipal or national law (i.e. it deliberately supplied no choice of law), is fully displaced, so no retained sentence contradicts the express New York selection.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: 27.2 confers "exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County" — both court levels and the correct county are named. No competing forum is carved out; the absence of a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out leaves the merits forum wholly exclusive and therefore no weaker than the element requires. The blocking sentence in 27.1 ("This procedure shall be the sole and exclusive remedy...") is replaced by "This procedure shall not limit any Party's right to bring the dispute before the courts specified in Subparagraph 27.2," so the retained Management Committee power to "determine the method, such as arbitration" cannot foreclose the New York courts; the escalation step survives only as a non-exclusive pre-court process.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect — the drafter elected the preferred level, which is complete.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Not a defect given the preferred level is satisfied.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: New York law is expressly chosen and exclusive merits jurisdiction is vested in the state and federal courts in New York County.

The 'deviation' classification is correct: the original document contained no choice of law at all (27.2 affirmatively instructed tribunals to ignore all connecting factors) and 27.1 made an internal committee procedure — which could impose arbitration by an unspecified method and seat — the sole and exclusive remedy, which fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory.

Minimality holds. 27.2 had no jurisdiction or forum words to swap, so a concise wholesale replacement is the least intrusive route for what is functionally a missing clause; retaining the old anti-choice-of-law sentence would have contradicted the new selection. The single edit to 27.1 is necessary rather than cosmetic: the retained 'sole and exclusive remedy' sentence would otherwise bar the very courts given exclusive jurisdiction, creating an internal inconsistency. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, damages category, or other extra was added.

Intent is preserved. The escalation duty, the Management Committee referral, its permissive reference to arbitration (cross-referenced by Paragraph 20), and the continued-performance-during-dispute sentence all survive unchanged, so no cross-reference is left dangling and no undefined term is introduced.

Residual point to watch (rationale-level, not a defect requiring repair): 27.1 still lets the Management Committee 'determine the method, such as arbitration.' The added non-limitation sentence subordinates any such determination to the parties' court right, so exclusivity stands; if the counterparty resists, consider adding 'subject to Subparagraph 27.2' to that determination power rather than expanding the redline now.

Optional refinement, not required for completeness: the clause omits the customary carve-out permitting applications for temporary injunctive relief in other courts. Its absence strengthens exclusivity for us, so no change is needed.
